To: group:levy-longsight-noticeboard
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Blue pills: what to do if someone goes down (please read, and please share)

I'm a nurse in intensive care in Manchester and I can't sleep, so I'm putting this up as its own post rather than adding it to the Saturday thread.

I've read the thread. I'm not going to speculate about who was there or what happened, because families have been through enough and guessing helps nobody. But rumour and slagging kids off is not what stops this happening again. So this is what I know, and what I'd do.

The police warning Gaz shared on Friday is the most useful thing on this noticeboard right now. Blue tablets being sold as diazepam or Xanax. Some of them have nitazenes in them, which are synthetic opioids, and some of those are way stronger than heroin. The police have been clear about their priority: preserving life. Please read that post properly, it's worth the minute it takes.

Signs that someone has taken something bad:

- extreme drowsiness, hard to wake up
- pinpoint pupils (tiny black dots in the middle of the eye)
- slow or noisy breathing
- blue lips

If any of that is happening, ring 999 straight away. Now, not in ten minutes.

What not to do: don't put them to bed to sleep it off. Don't wait to see if they wake up fine. Don't watch their breathing for an hour and then decide. I know that's the instinct, the family's in the front room, it's the small hours, you don't want to make a fuss. But if someone's breathing has gone slow and noisy, by the time you ring hours later their brain's been without oxygen for too long and the damage is already done. That delay is the whole reason people die from this.

And ring anyway. You will not be in trouble. The police don't want your house and they don't want whoever sold it, they want the person breathing. Say what you saw and that's it.

If you want to try something while you're waiting for the ambulance: naloxone nasal spray reverses opioids. Brightpath on Stockport Road (next to the launderette) do free kits. Anyone can walk in and ask, no names needed. Training takes about ten minutes and they'll show you how to use it. Open Mon-Fri 10-4, Thursdays till 7.

Two asks, and they're the important ones.

1. Parents, talk to your kids this week. This week, not after half term, not "when things are calmer". I did it with my lad (14) over tea last night. He rolled his eyes at me the entire time and then asked me what pinpoint pupils meant. He was listening. He just didn't want me to know he was listening.

2. Please share this, don't just like it. Send it to the school chat, the parents' WhatsApp, your own family group. Likes don't keep anybody alive. One forward does.

On slagging the kids off: a scared kid doesn't ring for help, and that's the whole problem. If your child is frightened of being shouted at, of getting in trouble, of you finding out, they will sit on it and go quiet, and that's when it goes wrong. I'd rather my lad rolled his eyes at me for ten minutes than not tell me something.

If you're not sure whether someone's breathing properly, ring 999 and then message me on here. I'll answer. I'll be awake anyway.
